title: Slow-wave sleep peaks in early childhood and drops in the teenage years
summary: NHLBI says slow-wave sleep peaks in early childhood, drops sharply in the teenage years, and may be absent in older people.
body: The stages page follows the newborn REM note with a second age pattern. The amount of slow-wave sleep peaks in early childhood and then drops sharply in the teenage years. It continues to decrease through adulthood, and older people may not have any slow-wave sleep at all. NHLBI is describing a typical shift across ages. It is not a test result for one child, and a missing stretch of deep sleep on one night is not what this sentence measures.

sources.title: How Sleep Works: Sleep Phases and Stages
sources.author: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
